question.text: Rekha is assessing an AIF whose PPM commits to a healthcare-focused strategy. During DD she finds 30% of the portfolio is in real estate and 20% in technology. This finding is BEST described as:

answer.text: Potential style drift / actions inconsistent with the PPM's investment strategy and sector focus, requiring comparison of portfolio composition with the PPM and review of any material change to objectives or strategy
Proof that the fund manager is better than sector specialists

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook requires PPM disclosure of investment strategy and sector exposure, supports caps on investee-company and sector exposure, and flags style drift and actions inconsistent with fund documentation as well as material changes to investment objectives/strategy. Comparing the actual portfolio composition with the PPM's stated healthcare focus is exactly the workbook's style-drift test. The Trap: Diversification is generally positive, but when it contradicts the stated strategy it is a breach of the investment mandate, not a strength. Note: The workbook does not set a numeric "off-strategy" threshold — any material divergence from the PPM's stated sector focus should trigger a style-drift review and a check for board-approved strategy changes.
